sections.what_happened: United Torah Judaism (7 seats: Degel HaTorah 4, Agudat Yisrael 3) declined to recommend any candidate for prime minister during consultations with President Isaac Herzog, withholding support from longtime ally Benjamin Netanyahu, after both factions were instructed by their spiritual leaders not to endorse a candidate. The decision leaves Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot with a clear lead in recommendations — 56 lawmakers vs Netanyahu's 46 — as Herzog continues consultations. UTJ said its support for any future government will depend on legislation preserving yeshiva military-service exemptions; the break follows frustration with Netanyahu for not passing that legislation. Consultations continue through Thursday evening (Yashar 7:15 p.m., Likud 8:30 p.m. Israel time); the Joint List has not declared whom it will support.
sections.what_verified: Times of Israel (T3) reports the decision itself; Haaretz (T3) corroborates the 56/46 tally and the prior expectation. Single family for the decision event; tally corroborated by a second family.
sections.what_disputed: UTJ's abstention does not hand Eisenkot a majority: 56 recommendations is short of the 61-seat Knesset majority; the Joint List (11 seats) has not declared, and Lieberman (Yisrael Beiteinu) refuses a government reliant on Arab-party support. Herzog is not legally required to give the mandate to the candidate with the most recommendations. A minority-government route (49-46 with abstentions, per Ynet via Azernews) remains unconfirmed and faces the same conscription-exemption obstacle.
sections.why_matters: Netanyahu loses his ultra-Orthodox ally: the 7-seat party that propped him up now refuses to back him — 56 vs 46. Israeli domestic coalition politics, NOT in the proven set (owner lock 2026-10-26); monitor only, no production slot unless Herzog's mandate decision creates a government-formation outcome with a war-policy consequence.
